title: Vietnamese Beef Pho
subtitle: Aromatic beef broth with rice noodles and fresh herbs
excerpt: A long-simmered beef broth spiced with star anise, cloves, and charred ginger is the heart of pho. Ladle it over rice noodles and finish with fresh herbs and lime at the table.
sourceNotes: Pho originated in northern Vietnam in the early 20th century and spread throughout the country after 1954. The broth is the defining element and takes time to develop its depth of flavour.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the broth only, without the noodles or garnishes. Defrost overnight and reheat to a rolling boil before serving.
recipe.batchNotes: Make a large batch of broth and freeze in portions. Cook noodles fresh each time.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The broth improves after a night in the fridge. Skim the fat from the surface before reheating.

content.text: Char the onion and ginger first. This gives the broth a smoky, sweet flavour. Do it over a gas flame or under a hot grill.

items.prepNote: flat rice noodles, soaked in cold water for 30 minutes before cooking

content.text: Char the cut sides of the onion and ginger halves. Hold them over a gas flame using tongs, or place under a hot grill, until blackened in patches. Set aside.
Put the brisket in the stockpot. Cover with cold water and bring to the boil. Boil for 5 minutes, then drain. Rinse the meat and the pot.
Return the brisket to the pot. Add the beef stock and 500ml of water.
Add the charred onion and ginger. Add the star anise, cloves, and cinnamon.
Bring to the boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer. Skim any foam from the surface.
Simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours until the brisket is tender enough to slice easily.
Remove the brisket and slice thinly across the grain. Strain the broth and discard the solids.
Return the broth to the pot. Season with fish sauce and soy sauce. Taste and adjust.
Cook the soaked noodles in boiling water for 1 to 2 minutes until just tender. Drain and divide among bowls.
Lay sliced brisket over the noodles. Ladle over the very hot broth.
Scatter with spring onion and coriander. Serve with lime wedges and sliced chilli on the side.

items.cause: Brisket was not blanched before simmering, or the simmer is too vigorous.
items.fix: Keep the heat very low; the surface should barely tremble.

items.symptom: Broth tastes flat despite long cooking.
items.cause: Not enough fish sauce, or stock was low-quality.
items.fix: Add fish sauce a tablespoon at a time until the depth builds.

items.cause: Drained and left to sit before serving.
items.fix: Rinse under hot water to loosen them before adding broth.
